events.title: Death of Alexander the Great
events.description: Alexander III of Macedon died in Babylon at about age 32, according to the traditional dating of June 10 or 11, 323 BCE. His death followed a brief illness, and the cause remains debated by historians.
events.significance: His death ended the reign of one of history's most successful military commanders and led to the fragmentation of his empire among the Diadochi, shaping the Hellenistic world.

events.title: First Hanging of the Salem Witch Trials
events.description: Bridget Bishop was hanged at Proctor's Ledge in Salem, Massachusetts, after being convicted of witchcraft. She was the first person executed in the Salem witch trials.
events.significance: Her execution began a wave of hysteria that led to the executions of 19 people and became a lasting symbol of the dangers of mass paranoia and unjust legal proceedings.

events.title: Alcoholics Anonymous Founded
events.description: Bill Wilson and Dr. Bob Smith held what is regarded as the founding date of Alcoholics Anonymous in Akron, Ohio, when Dr. Bob had his last drink on June 10, 1935.
events.significance: AA grew into a worldwide fellowship with millions of members and pioneered the twelve-step model of peer-support recovery from addiction.

events.title: Italy Declares War on Britain and France
events.description: Benito Mussolini announced that Italy would enter World War II on the side of Nazi Germany, with the declaration taking effect on June 11, as German forces advanced through France.
events.significance: Italy's entry expanded the war into the Mediterranean and North Africa, opening new theaters of conflict and ultimately contributing to the fall of Mussolini's regime.

events.title: Apple II Computer Goes on Sale
events.description: Apple Computer began shipping the Apple II, one of the first highly successful mass-produced personal computers, with color graphics and an open architecture.
events.significance: The Apple II helped launch the personal computer industry and brought computing into homes and schools.
